long_biography.plain_text:
Golisano spotted an overlooked market while selling payroll services to large employers: most businesses were small, but established providers ignored them. After executives rejected his plan, he used $3,000 and a credit card to launch Paychex in 1971. By packaging payroll as an affordable recurring service and growing through franchises and joint ventures, he built a national client base. The company entered public markets in 1983.

He led Paychex as president and chief executive for 33 years, then remained chairman and subsequently a director. The company developed into a technology-driven provider of payroll and human-capital services. After leaving its board, Golisano concentrated on startup investments, private-company directorships, entrepreneurship education and philanthropy. Those activities extend the founder's capital and experience but remain distinct from the payroll-services business that created his wealth.
